steps.text: Shangshu, Great Cold, Year 507, light snow.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Yo, there you are.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: We have an agreement.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: One hundred whole days.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: The snow on the way held one up by some nights. I would be here even earlier otherwise.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Must have what I wanted if you're back so soon, then?

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: It has been brought. The spiciest pepper in all of Shangshu.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Looks like you did a pretty good job. Can't have been easy finding something this fresh through months of snowstorms.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: You've crouched hidden, sir, for years on years, and yet you know of blizzards in the human realm?

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Oh? Sounds like you're getting at something.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Shangshu's mountains wind long and hard; there's always someplace to shelter from the winds.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: One traveled all over the Three Mounts and Eighteen Peaks, visiting every household and inn, sampling one by one...

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: You know what, save the story. Kitchen's over that way, ingredients and utensils are all there. Get your cook on.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Please have a taste, sir.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Oh? What, just simple shuizhu?

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Even so, not many in Shangshu would afford this dish these days.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Neat. I'll give it a try.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: What do you... think, sir?

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Heh. It's a fundamental truth that the slices of meat in shuizhu all have to be equally thick, but you've even cut them all to identical form—I have to compliment the knifework. But...

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Tsk. It's not got much flavor.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: If this is the spiciest pepper you could find in all of Shangshu, then I'm sorry to say the sword can't go to you.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Sir—!

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: One doesn't seek your sword for her own selfish desires, but in petition for the common folk! I beg you—

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: It doesn't matter to me why you want the sword. If the chili's not good, then you're not having it.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: I've had enough for today. Go on home.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: But a moment, please.
The swordsman draws the dagger holstered on her side, and cuts open her wrist with not a pause of hesitation. Fresh, her carmine blood drips into the stew.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Why not see, sir... if the taste satisfies you now?

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: That's fun.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Take it.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Shangshu's spiciest pepper, in exchange for Shangshu's finest blade. The fairest trade.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: My thanks, sir!

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Don't thank me, we made an agreement. That's business.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Something else on your mind?

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: You give me this sword so reassured, and don't even ask what I would use it for?

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Doesn't matter to me if you cut firewood, heads or a mean deal at the pawn shop, so long as after a hundred days, you hand it back to me.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: If I were to break it, carelessly...

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: If anything in this world could break that sword, I'd like to see it.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: If...

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: If you've got regrets, you can just give it back to me now.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: No... I swear on my soul. In a hundred days, I will return it as it came to me.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Alright, you can get out of my sight now. Down the mountain you go.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: My thanks, sir. One has her greatest gratitude.

steps.name: Swordsmith
steps.text: Interesting, seriously interesting...

steps.name: 'Hat of the Ink'
steps.text: 'A fine sword... and fine technique.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Wrngh... huff... huff...
Marvelous, marvelous... that was truly beyond belief.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: What don't you believe? That a blind woman could outspeed your 'Hat of the Ink's' blade, or that someone out there existed who could forge a sword to fell yours?

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Ke Luxi of the Twilight... you've lost...

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Uh-huh. Have I, now?

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: You said that to anyone who could produce a sword stronger than yours, you would tell how you make the 'Divine Meteonite.' Now, it's time you made good on your pledge.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Ha, I did say so... but I'm wondering. With a weapon that exceptional, do you even still need my formula?

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: The need is not mine, but the people of Shangshu's.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: A Catastrophe passed through, and many are displaced. Shangshu is troubled. If they had the 'Divine Meteonite,' safe shelter from the elements could be built that much faster.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Sir K'o, our mutual contention is but a thing of the past. No further argument, nor hate, supersedes the common folk. A victor in this duel of swords is clear. In mind and heart, you ought to—

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Hahahaha... trust a hero to worry over the nation and her people. Sorry to tell you...

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: You were too naive. There was never such a thing as 'Divine Meteonite'.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: What did you say?!

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Let me ask you a question now, about that sword. Did it come from Zuanjiang Peak? From a red-horned and red-eyed swordsmith?

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: How do you know—

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Heh. I figured you'd only find one swordsmith in all of Yan with a fighting chance against me.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Ke Luxi, you did all this just to...

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Correct. I just couldn't understand! My swordsmithing technique is apex, it's peak! So how does it still not beat hers?!

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: I've been tossing and turning this past decade, dying just to get my hands on a sword of her own making. I'll research it, engineer it, figure out just what kind of art went into making it!

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: I should really thank you for coming all this way, just to drop her sword off with us.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Now, be nice and give up the goods, and I'll let you go.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: So be it...

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: This complete swindle isn't worth arguing with you over. If there never was any 'Divine Meteonite,' then I don't want to bother with you for even a second longer.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: And yet this sword's time with me is borrowed. I must return it as agreed. I can't let you take it.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: You don't know what's good for you... Forth!

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: What's a single fine swordswoman's limit? How many does it take? Ready!

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: (Gasp)

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Still not willing to listen to me? Then you asked for it.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Fire—
Tsk. That's just embarrassing, Ke Luxi. If you love my swords so much, you could always say it to my face. Why waste all your effort, and this li'l lady's?
Just concede, and I'll give you all you could want. I can even sign the hilts for you.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Nian Huihan! What are you doing here?!

steps.name: Nian Huihan
steps.text: I finally caught a break for ten years. Now I have to find just who cares about me so much, and it turns out it's you after all.

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: Sir...

steps.name: Nian Huihan
steps.text: And you, you're honest to a fault. It's one sword, that's all. If they wanted it, you could've just given it to them. Why get yourself hurt in the process?

steps.name: Yi
steps.text: I told you, I swore on my soul...

steps.name: Nian Huihan
steps.text: Hah. I'll admit, that's just like you.

steps.name: Nian Huihan
steps.text: But first. Now that I'm here, no sword or its warrior should be trying any more funny business.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: S... Seize them!

steps.name: Nian Huihan
steps.text: Heavenly forge—

steps.name: Nian Huihan
steps.text: So that's it? Let's pull out any last tricks we've got on the count of three.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: ...I truly do hate your lofty guts. Since the day I lost to you ten years ago, I've vowed in secret to make you pay the price for your arrogance.

steps.name: Nian Huihan
steps.text: What can you do? You put up some tepid competition for our line of work. I couldn't even muster much of my own drive.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Heheh... Nian Huihan, you're too conceited. You thought no one under Heaven could match you in the art of the forge, and so you fossilized.

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: This is the day you regret laying about for the last ten years! I'll show you the leaps and bounds my metallurgy has taken!

steps.name: Ke Luxi
steps.text: Come forth, Archbeast Mechanica!

steps.name: Archbeast Mechanica
steps.text: (Screeching) Diiii—didiiii—

steps.name: Archbeast Mechanica
steps.text: (Furious roaring) Diiiii—

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: C—Cut!!!

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: What? C'mon, we're just about to hit the climax.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Why does every single one of your movies have to end with a giant kaiju?!

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Huh? 'Cause it's cooler that way, duh.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: But isn't this meant to be Yanese wuxia?!

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Don't let genres box in your thinking. Kung fu, suspense, sci-fi... the more marketing elements, the better, yeah?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: You should hire Whisperain as a literary consultant before you ever touch another screenplay...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: And you're going to drag Closure in to play the villain? Since when does she have the time to humor your nonsense?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: And! Also! I've wanted to roast you for this since the beginning! You always say I'm the lead, so why do you keep stealing the spotlight at all the key moments?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Aww, don't be so petty. The big sacrifice scene in the climax is all yours.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I die in this?!

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: The character, the character dies.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: What are you calling this one? 'Call of the Deadly Swordswoman' or 'Forged in Berserk?'

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: 'Ruthless Sword vs. the Queen of the Machines.'

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I'm begging you now, don't slap Rhodes Island's name on this movie when you distribute it or all our partner firms are going to question our taste.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Sure, everyone's a critic these days, but do you know how much cash Wrankwood rakes in each year on these kinds of movies?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Convinced now?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I've given up...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I shouldn't be wasting my free time listening to you read these stories.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I have training this afternoon. I'm off.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Remember to come back to hear the ending.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Like hell I will!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Wait a moment, I have one more question...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: What parts of this story were true?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Huh? Where's that coming from?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: The story sounds stupid to the max overall, but I also feel like—some details didn't feel completely made-up...

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Oh? So what do you think? Which parts sound real to you?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Was there really a blind swordswoman?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Caught your interest?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Are you going to tell me or not?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: No matter what 'the truth' is, it can only be 'stories' once you're hearing it. How can asking if 'stories' are true not be self-contradictory?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Forget it, I'm sure you made it all up at random. Why should I care...?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Bye.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Wait, wait, I was gonna let you stay on as director!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Count me out until you come up with a screenplay even slightly more normal!

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: *Sigh* Maybe I'm too avant garde for modern audiences to understand... I guess they'll catch up, sooner or later.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: But I've got all this stuff to prep in advance, and if li'l Lava's not with me, I'm not gonna get it done on my own.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I heard people turned dour as they became older. Not that I believed it until now.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Did the trip to Shangshu make you miss someone?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: What d'you think? You'd say it's a touching story too, wouldn't you?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I have no interest in wasting time criticizing your turgid film scripts... Did you grind my entire evening to a halt just to make me read this?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Fine, I've read it all. Now stop bothering me, and get out.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: What else do you want?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I want to invite you to do some storyboarding and concept art.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Dream on!

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I swear, I am going to incinerate every last one of your garbage films while you sleep.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: You're all grown up now. Why do you still act out like such a kid?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: How many years has it been?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: What was that?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Don't be stupid.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Why does this sound like you've seen straight through my story?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Being too easily understood's kind of its own blow to an author, you know.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Too bad we've known each other for so long, 'big sis.'

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I did genuinely want to look through the Sui Regulator's criminal records, just to see what kind of mortifying history you left behind.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: You and li'l Lava are two peas in a pod with your tempers. Always gotta pretend like you don't care, even when you're so obviously curious.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Let me be clear. I haven't the slightest interest in your lousy screenplay, but I do want to know what you're dwelling on so miserably that you wrote this entire scenario as a roundabout homage.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Sure. Put on some tea, and we can chat nice and easy.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: You have to tell it as it was... No garnishes allowed.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Haha... really, I couldn't tell you which year or month it was. I only remember nomadic cities didn't exist yet.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: And I remember, it was snowing that day.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Even without the year, I know I finally had enough of that tomb, and thought I'd head up to the surface to kill my boredom.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: But it was ordinary sights everywhere I looked. Came out, and it was all the same as when I went in.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: And I thought to myself, y'know, in the end, this is all people are. You make a crowd of a million fight for a moment of glory in the battlesands, but their lives only amount to a couple decades in the end. What are they ever gonna contribute?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I was just passing the time, wandering wherever. But the Sui Regulator sure didn't like me idle, so they dumped an errand on me, had me head to Shangshu just after a Catastrophe hit, help the locals rebuild the city.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: The Sui Regulator has a lot of confidence sending you on these jobs.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: It's pretty much where my role lands, right? I'm specialized for it.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: So you worked obediently?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: You bet I didn't.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: How brazen of you.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: *Sigh* I can't say I totally slacked, but the terrain in Shangshu was vicious stuff at the time. Even if I took it seriously, drumming up a three-story building would be a heck of a lot of effort.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: But what the Sui Regulator specified was to 'build a city that can withstand a small Catastrophe.' They just wanted to weigh me down on purpose, right?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: So, I went as I felt, helped with some small stuff sometimes, gave a demo or two.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Shangshu's food really hit the spot for me, so I didn't mind staying for a while.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Until one day...

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Some kid found out where I lived, and begged me to make a sword.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I guess I wasn't too low-key living in Shangshu. Made sense I left a legend or two behind. But I didn't expect... Oripathy to take both his eyes.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Honestly, you've been here for days. What exactly are you thinking?

steps.name: Young Swordsman
steps.text: Sir, I only wish for you to grant me a sword. One is ready to pay any price in exchange.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Sounds fine, but what price can you afford? Besides, what do you want a sword for?

steps.name: Young Swordsman
steps.text: To save. To avenge.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Gah... that's a headache.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: No matter how I asked, he just answered the same four words, 'to save, to avenge'—but I didn't even care, to be honest.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I got seriously sick of him and just forged him a random sword. And he'd never be able to afford it, in any scenario, so I could only lend it to him. He'd have to give it back in a hundred days.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: After about three months, I practically forgot about it when one day, out of nowhere, an old guy came calling.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I knew him. He was the owner of an inn at the edge of the city.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: He gave me a bundle, with a broken sword wrapped inside.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: What's this?

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: A child gave me some money, and asked me to deliver this to the swordsmith living on Zuanjiang Peak.

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: *Sigh*... We've had spring chills for the last few days, and snow. It's a treacherous road up here, I tell you...

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: He told you to give to me? Why didn't he come himself?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Ohh... he broke it, so he's too shy to see me in person?

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: I suppose he's... passed on by now...

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Why—did he die?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I've got no idea.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: What? Did that old man not tell you?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: He told me he did what the youngster said, went to a specific place at a specific time to pick up the sword. He got there, and he saw nothing but burnt-out ruins.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Who knows how long it was burning, but nothing in there was recognizable anymore. Just that broken sword lying in the middle, nothing else.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I'm beginning to feel as if you're spinning a tale again.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Aw, that's just uncalled for. Can't you even have the most basic trust in your sister here?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: What happened next?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Nothing to speak of. I didn't ask much more, and frankly, I wasn't the least bit interested.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I cast that broken sword back into a new billet, and had the old guy take it down for the city craftsmen to use.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: If that material could teach them a thing or two, I was sure it'd improve their tech, so I considered myself even with the Sui Regulator.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: You get bored staying too long in one place, so after that, I left Shangshu.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: And there I thought to myself, I gave them some pointers, helped them improve their art; they ought to realize Shangshu's not suitable for long-term habitation, and go find another home. Acceptable ending, by and large.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Until fifty years later, I went back to Shangshu again.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: And in those towering mountains, I found a city.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: The Three Mounts and Eighteen Peaks of Shangshu. Rugged place to put passes through, and the plank walkways people set up were just one death road after another; the peaks were steep, yet they'd have a tower built at the crowning summits.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I obviously could've taken the credit, thought how if I didn't give them any tips, it'd be anyone's guess, the years they'd polish their tech to reach that level of understanding.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: But the sight of those vast walls in the sunlight, I was honestly just stunned. Not a thought like that ever came to me.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I never expected to hear you say anything like that.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Maybe that was the moment my thinking changed.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: People. They really are neat after all.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Is that the end?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I guess so.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: If you have to be technical, there's still a tiny little epilogue...

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Anybody home?

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Come in, come right in! Sit anywhere you like!

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: 'Xingcheng Inn'... Was that always this place's name?

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: You may not know, but they say that fifty years ago, Shangshu went through a Catastrophe.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: My grandpa brought in divine metal from a god, and that was the metal our craftsmen built the modern Shangshu with.

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: My grandpa wanted to commemorate it, so he changed the name of the shop to 'Xingcheng', just like our new city rising.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: That's neat. Then did your grandpa ever tell you the prequel to that story?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Like, about a blind swordsman, maybe a broken blade?

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: You're a funny one, ma'am. The god's metal's just a legend, no more. Where's a swordsman breaking anything come from?

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: If you want to hear about fifty years ago, you'll have to find the storyteller in the teahouse. It'll cost you a pretty penny to listen to his nonsense, too.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Yeah, you're right. It was fifty years ago.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Whatever, I'm just rambling... hey, boss, I'll have some shuizhu, extra spicy!

steps.name: Innkeeper
steps.text: Coming up! Just one moment.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Seriously...

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: It was just a sword...

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: By the sound of it, you regret it?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I kind of do.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Do you regret not giving that boy a better sword, or that you didn't go see for yourself just what ended him?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I regret not coming out a few years earlier.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: All those years buried in that pitch-black tomb. Really was a waste of time.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: And who knows how much time we have left, still.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: No matter what... you always come back to this topic.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Don't just shrug it off like that. Isn't this the biggest household argument our whole family's got?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I'm tired. I'm going to bed. Hurry up and leave.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: And since when did you start being able to sleep again?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Admit it, li'l sis. We're all still in a dream. It's so crammed with interesting stuff, it's got us forgetting just how fragile the dream really is.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: But we'll have to wake up at some point.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Suit yourself. How do you plan to take a dream out with you?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: First, find a way to make it carry on a little longer. If we're going to wake up no matter what, then I'd like to ready up a giant firecracker, and blow this dream apart with my own hands.
